content: Before starting levofloxacin and each time you refill your prescription, read the medication guide provided by your pharmacist. Take this medication orally on an empty stomach, either one hour before or two hours after eating, as directed by your doctor, typically once daily.g., antacids or calcium-enriched juice). The dosage and duration of treatment depend on your medical condition and response to therapy. For optimal results, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue taking it for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Stopping the medication early may allow bacteria to continue growing, potentially leading to a return of the infection. Common side effects may include nausea, diarrhea, headache, dizziness, lightheadedness, or trouble sleeping. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, levofloxacin may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridium difficile (C. difficile), which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after stopping the medication. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may also lead to oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. If you experience symptoms such as rash, itching/swelling (especially of the face/tongue/throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing, seek medical attention immediately. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Before taking levofloxacin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other quinolone antibiotics (e.g., ciprofloxacin, moxifloxacin, ofloxacin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Levofloxacin may rarely cause a condition affecting the heart rhythm (QT prolongation), which can increase the risk of serious irregular heartbeats. The risk may be higher if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that can cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood may also increase this risk, especially if you use certain medications (e.g., diuretics) or have conditions such as severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. Levofloxacin may rarely cause significant changes in blood sugar levels, particularly in individuals with diabetes. Monitor for symptoms of high blood sugar (e.g., increased thirst or urination) or low blood sugar (e.g., sudden sweating, shaking, fast heartbeat, hunger, blurred vision, dizziness, or tingling in the hands/feet). Carry glucose tablets or gel to treat low blood sugar. If unavailable, quickly raise your blood sugar by consuming sugar, honey, candy, fruit juice, or non-diet soda. Inform your doctor immediately about any reactions and the use of this medication. To prevent low blood sugar, eat meals on a regular schedule and avoid skipping meals. This drug may cause dizziness or lightheadedness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Levofloxacin may increase your sensitivity to sunlight. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). Children using this drug may have a higher risk of joint or tendon problems. During pregnancy, levofloxacin should only be used when clearly necessary. It passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Levofloxacin is very similar to ofloxacin, so avoid using ofloxacin-containing products while taking this medication. This drug may interfere with certain lab tests (e.g., urine screening for opiates), potentially causing false test results. If someone overdoses and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911. Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
